layers.does: What the assets pushed. One writer, so a real OEM feed swaps in unchanged.
layers.name: Asset telemetry

layers.does: Defines which actions are FEASIBLE. Blocked counts refusals the engine acted on; a failed advisory rule is recorded, not refused.
layers.name: Deterministic rules (L1)

layers.does: Reads the frame, picks an objective, writes bounded policy. Proposes; never disposes. Runs beside the tick and never holds it.
layers.name: Orchestrator agent

layers.does: Propose stall assignments for the kernel to dispose. CP-SAT is primary inside the site; cuOpt proposes as a fallback. Nondeterministic by nature, which is why L4 exists.
layers.name: Proposers

layers.does: Disposes every proposal. Refusing some is the point: all-enacted is a rubber stamp.
layers.name: Deterministic disposal

scanner.cadence: every minute, live operator and production runs

questions.asks: Retired 2026-09-27 (rule 9). It asked whether a fast charger was still filling a car above the deploy floor while other cars waited. A car charging to its own target is never a question, so no new episode is raised.
questions.lever: None. Ending a charge early is never a lever (rule 9). Cars waiting while chargers finish full charges is a capacity signal: more chargers, fewer faults, a charger freed the moment its car is done, better ordering of who is served next.
questions.grade_means: Its earlier grades say only that the car charged on while the longest waiter waited on. They never meant the charge should have ended.

questions.asks: A charger is free by every gate (pointer, calendar, session, charger state) while a car has waited five minutes or more.
questions.lever: A missed assignment. Graded before it earns a proposer seat.
questions.grade_means: A confirmed grade says a charger stayed free by every gate across two scans while the longest waiter waited 5 more minutes: a missed assignment.

questions.asks: A charger is faulted while cars wait for a charger.
questions.lever: Capacity lost to faults; the fault's duration is the grade.
questions.grade_means: A confirmed grade says the fault lasted 30 minutes or more while cars waited: charger capacity lost.

On dbdffd5c, 14 fast-charger sessions went to cars that wanted an L2 while a mean 9.4 low or immediate cars waited, and 46 cars that wanted a fast charger spent a mean 264 minutes on an L2. The treatment raises deployed car-hours without leaving any return unserved or moving the five KPIs more than 2% the wrong way. No charge is shortened (rule 9). Arms at 6 sim-minutes a tick from 8:00 AM CT for 90 ticks (to 5:00 PM, the operator governor's 540 sim-minute day).

experiments.why: Chase, 2026-09-27 (about 4:40 PM CT): a vehicle's needs are never sacrificed for site optimization; a charge is never stopped short of the vehicle's target except for a charger fault or a vehicle emergency (offline, service stall, long-term staging). This experiment tests stopping fast charges short to free chargers for waiting cars, so it is out of bounds whatever it would find. Its counted pairs stay in the pair ledger as evidence.
experiments.hypothesis: G263 (db/checks/0400 §5): a DCFC charge planned before 6:00 AM keeps the night ceiling (dcfc_target_soc_night, 100) for its whole session. On ad106e55 (busy_day from 5:03 AM CT) two cars whose own target is 100 arrived at 81%, above the 80% deploy floor, and charged to 100% for 85 and 88 minutes, 56 and 58 of them above 90% at a mean 9 kW, while 19-21 cars waited, 15 below the floor; the challenger graded both confirmed (Q1). A night ceiling of 90 frees those charger-minutes for the queue in the morning ramp. Pair 102 (0399) found the day target's cut can lose the day by sending cars out with less charge; this tests the slowest slice, above 90. Arms from 5:03 AM CT (57 night minutes) for 90 ticks at 6 sim-minutes, to 2:03 PM: the operator's window on ad106e55. The dial is not agent-writable, so a win is a recommendation. If it wins, the change to build is the ceiling in force when the charge would end (the plan still fixes it once), not a lower night dial: the arms never see the night's no-queue hours.

experiments.hypothesis: G255/G256 (db/checks/0397): the depot's binding resource on a busy day is DCFC time -- on 6e0352a0 at about 2 PM sim 28-29 cars waited a mean 185 minutes for a DCFC while 16 of the 36 charging cars were already between the 80% deploy floor and the 90% day target. Filling a daytime DCFC to 85% instead of 90% spends less charger time in the taper, so cars under the floor get a charger sooner and more of the work side's demand is met. 85 not 80: the charge atom closes at target-1, which stays above the deploy floor. First experiment run in the operator's world (0531).
